title: Initiative Handoff SLA and Dependency Ticketing Playbook
creator: Priya Malhotra
description: Context: As Redwood scales multi-quarter initiatives we see repeated last-minute blockers when design/infra/security artifacts lag engineering readiness. This ticket creates a lightweight operational SLA and ticketing pattern to ensure initiative handoffs include explicit dependency signals, owners, and automated gating. Goals: 1) Define an 'Initiative Handoff SLA' (timelines + artifact checklist) for PMs to mark work as ready for eng/design/security/infra. 2) Create a 'dependency ticket' archetype that auto-populates owners, required artifacts, and verification steps. 3) Integrate dependency signals into the quarterly planning board and as release gates. Non-goals: This is not a full workflow engine — initial scope focuses on conventions + automation in Linear and hooks to existing Confluence and GitHub. Trade-offs: We deliberately keep the SLA tight (T-6 weeks for major infra/security artifacts) to reduce surprise, accepting more frontloaded work for teams. Alternative of fully automated enforcement via CI was rejected for now due to infra effort and cross-org resistance. Links: Confluence design doc - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Initiative+Handoff+SLA ; Draft ticket archetype - https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HandoffTicketArchetype; Prototype GH action to tag dependency tickets - https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2481
